name: leaderboard
title: Leaderboard
description: Ranked rows with a pinned "you" row and a designed empty case. The row carries `data-gs-rank` and the score inside it is a `stat` carrying `data-gs-value`, because one element's value cannot carry two numbers. Rank movement is the sign of `data-gs-delta`: there is no trend attribute. Rows travel to their new places over the reorder token and stop dead under reduced motion, where the order is still correct because it is the DOM order. The pinned row is the same row with a second marker, not a second component. Performs nothing: the host owns the order, the paging and who moved.
docs: Hand `entries` over already ranked; this never sorts and never pages. Set `you` on the player's entry and a pinned copy of that row is held on screen, marked `data-gs-pinned`; pass `pinYou={false}` where the board is short enough not to need it. Set `delta` to the signed number of places a row just moved and the badge and the colour follow the sign. A reordering list is a screen-reader trap, so the list itself is not a live region: one polite status announces the player's own rank change and nothing else. An empty board renders `data-gs-empty="true"` with a designed empty case; pass `emptyAction` to give it the next step. Player names are rendered as text, never as markup. Installs into `components/gamestage/leaderboard/` rather than flat beside the others, so that its relative import of `stat` resolves to the same file in an installed app as it does in this repo. Changing the target to a flat file breaks that import. Inside a stage whose space is fixed it shows the top five by default, then a gap and the player's own row if they are further down, and a See all button, which shows every row in place, or calls `onSeeAll` so the host can open them in its own Sheet; pass `limit` to set the number, or 'all' to show every row. GSUI-282.
